title: Austronesian sea trade reaches South Asia
place: Maritime Southeast Asia to South Asia
summary: Austronesian sailors of Island Southeast Asia set up spice and crop trade links with southern India and Sri Lanka, spreading outrigger boats and plants such as coconut and banana.
why: The Indian Ocean became the 'cradle' of global trade, linking Asia, Arabia and Africa for millennia.

notes.problem: 3000 BCE impossible: Austronesians reached northern Philippines c. 2200 BCE; links to South India and Sri Lanka c. 1500-600 BCE.
